memories.text: I share a flat in Milan near the Navigli, and the aperitivo crowd outside is loud but fun.
I manage the e-commerce roadmap at Brera Fashion House, and fashion week is pure chaos.
I'm a product manager, which mostly means saying no to people nicely.
An Aperol spritz at seven is my favourite ritual, and the bartender downstairs knows it.
I prefer tables over prose whenever you compare options.
The allergist confirmed I'm not allergic to dust mites, my sneezing is just the city air.
My sister Giulia lives in Naples and refuses to admit Milan has good pizza.
Our product sync is on Tuesday mornings, right after the leadership call.
Quarterly roadmap review: collect feature requests, score them with RICE, and share the top ten with engineering.
On the side I'm advising Volta, a project building an e-scooter sharing app.
Volta is still at the wireframe stage, we're testing paper prototypes.
I joined the Navigli Running Club, we run along the canals at 6:30.
Hiked between the villages of Cinque Terre and ate focaccia at every stop.
Sadly I'm allergic to pistachios, so no Sicilian desserts for me.
For risotto I toast the carnaroli, add warm stock a ladle at a time, and finish with cold butter off the heat.
Correction: product sync moved to Thursday mornings to avoid the leadership call.
My sister's baby shower is happening at a villa in Como.
Volta is owned by the Piedmont Transit Consortium, who also run the trams.
Volta is blocked because the payment provider pulled out at the last minute.
Spent three days at Milan Design Week collecting brochures I'll never read.
The baby shower moved to Bergamo, the Como villa double-booked.
Our cat sleeps on my laptop keyboard every morning and sends random emails.
I've never had a driving licence, the metro has always been enough.
Remind me to renew my identity card before the end of March.
We moved to Turin in June, and the mountains at the end of every street are unreal.
I joined Lingotto Mobility in June as head of product.
Lingotto Mobility is headquartered in Genoa, by the old port.
I report to Paolo Ricci, the chief operating officer.
Paolo lives in Bologna and works from home on Fridays.
I signed up for the Turin marathon in November, terrifying.
I've given up alcohol, so chinotto over ice is my evening drink now.
Volta now has 10,000 riders, and the city wants to expand the zones.
Spent a week in Athens over New Year and climbed the Acropolis at dawn.
Finished the Turin marathon in 4:05, and I could not walk the next day.
Packing samples for trade fairs: steam everything, bag them by season, and label every hanger.
I've never been to the UK, which is embarrassing for a product person.
I'm hooked on audiobooks of Italian noir on my commute.
Remind me to book the running club trip before the 1st of September.
